title: 16 March 1970: Playback: McCartney by Paul McCartney
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, Abbey Road
Producer: Paul McCartney

Paul McCartney had finished recording his debut album McCartney on 25 February 1970. From then he prepared artwork and the release schedule.

On this day, 16 March, he returned to Abbey Road to listen to a playback of the recordings. It was a brief session, lasting from 6.30-8pm. Like all the other McCartney sessions, it was booked under the pseudonym Billy Martin.

The only song listened to on this occasion was ‘Oo You’. McCartney listened to both the eight-track and stereo mix, which had been previously prepared at Morgan Studios.

Page last updated: 1 April 2025

Also on this day...

  • 1993: Paul McCartney live: Sydney Entertainment Centre, Sydney
  • 1977: Recording: B Side To Seaside by Suzy And The Red Stripes
  • 1973: John Lennon and Ringo Starr watch Last Tango In Paris
  • 1972: Recording: Loup (1st Indian On The Moon) by Wings
  • 1972: John Lennon and Yoko Ono attend US Immigration hearing
  • 1971: Paul McCartney attends the 13th Annual Grammy Awards
  • 1971: Recording: Ram by Paul and Linda McCartney
  • 1969: Paul and Linda McCartney begin their honeymoon
  • 1965: Filming: Help!, Austria
  • 1964: US single release: Can’t Buy Me Love
  • 1964: Filming: A Hard Day’s Night
  • 1963: The Beatles live: City Hall, Sheffield
  • 1963: Radio: Saturday Club
  • 1962: The Beatles live: Cavern Club, Liverpool (evening)
  • 1961: The Beatles live: Cavern Club, Liverpool (lunchtime)
